claim_boundary: A strong result supports same-checkpoint, new-initial-condition evaluation replication of lower average H200 direct-rollout MSE for the joint soft-thresholding-plus-L1 sparse recipe. This is not retraining and not physics or system generalization. It does not repair the failed original four-cell gate, establish terminal superiority, attribute the effect to one sparse component, connect support alignment causally to forecasting, or establish performance beyond this Allen--Cahn system.

development_context.comparison_policy: show beside prospective aggregate only; never pool or call the opened result confirmatory
development_context.role: opened development evidence; permanently excluded from this replication

figure_caption: Same-checkpoint Allen--Cahn new-initial-condition replication. At H=200 (physical time T=20), the joint sparse recipe lowers mean direct-rollout field MSE over steps 1--200 by 5.86% across three new 256-trajectory datasets (ten paired model seeds; 95% paired-seed bootstrap CI 2.40--9.21%; exact one-sided sign-flip p=0.0088). Dataset-specific effects are descriptive and all positive. H200 terminal error is descriptive. Opened development and prospective results are shown separately and never pooled. Checkpoints were neither retrained nor reselected.
mandatory_disclosure: If every strong gate passes, report prospective new-initial-condition replication of lower H200 through-horizon direct-rollout MSE for the joint sparse recipe. Regardless of this branch, the original four-cell gate remains failed; both original terminal 95% paired-seed CIs crossed zero (H160 [-1.63%, 5.96%], H200 [-0.80%, 6.70%]); the original H200 terminal reduction was 3.22% with 7/10 seed wins, missing both 5% and 8/10 gates. This is an outcome-aware, endpoint-specific prospective replication of H200 through-horizon MSE, not a reclassification of the original experiment.
not_supported: repair of the original failed four-cell gate
